subject: Post-demo: Novacare qualification — model hitlist & fn-call/schema next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Jun 2029 17:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo: Novacare qualification — model hitlist & fn-call/schema next steps

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum.

1) Summary of fit
- Primary use case: structured extraction + rule-based routing from intake forms, followed by downstream scoring and short summarization for clinicians. Latency SLO: 200ms p50 for short requests; 95th under 800ms.
- Data sensitivity: PHI in snippets; Novacare wants VPC or dedicated capacity for production.

2) Proposed model hitlist for evaluation (priority order)
- redwood-raven-13b-q4 (cost-efficient; good for strict JSON schema compliance when paired with function-calling)
- redwood-apex-70b-fp16 (best quality for long-context extraction tasks; higher cost, use for edge-case validation)
- community-llama-3-13b-8k (baseline for throughput/latency comparison)

3) Evaluation assets attached
- novacare_prompt_set_v1.json — seed prompts and structured examples we used in the demo
- fncall_schema_v1.json — recommended function-call contract for your intake schema (fields, types, retry hints)
- novacare_eval_summary.pdf — compact summary of our benchmark runs from the demo environment

4) Key asks / next steps
- Can you confirm which environments we should run the canary in (Hosted vs Dedicated)?
- Please share the procurement contact so we can align on timing for Dedicated capacity if you want to proceed.
- We recommend a 48h canary run with two model variants (raven-13b-q4 + apex-70b-fp16) using your production-like sample; can Monica run the job with your sample once procurement gives the go-ahead?

5) Quality/regression note
- We flagged two failure modes during demo: (a) partial JSON output when prompts are ambiguous; (b) schema drift when input includes unexpected tokens. Our suggested mitigations: stricter schema validation on the agent side, fallback to re-prompt with explicit field anchors, and a short-circuit to the smaller model for highly repetitive/templated inputs.

If that sounds right I'll schedule the canary and include a short runbook for retries and schema validation.

Best,
Naomi Feldman

Alex / team — quick technical notes to address Alex's questions and to make the canary reproducible: 

- Re: null/partial JSON behavior
  * First line of defense: validate against fncall_schema_v1.json on receipt. If schema validation fails and the returned payload is >70% complete, attempt an automated re-call with a validation-anchored prompt (we prepend explicit field anchors and a maximum token length).
  * If after 2 automated retries the response still fails validation, mark for human review via your ticket queue (we can wire to your existing endpoint).
  * Implement an exponential backoff between retries: 500ms, 1s. Max 2 retries. This balances latency and cost.

- Idempotency pattern
  * Recommend request id composed as: novacare.{account}.{date}.{sha1(short_payload)} — use this as the function-call invocation id; store as token in your downstream processing to avoid double writes on replays.

- Canary plan (technical)
  * Step 0: confirm dataset sample (one JSONL with 1k samples; please strip PII where possible)
  * Step 1: run raven-13b-q4 across the sample with prefix caching on similar forms enabled (8 parallel workers)
  * Step 2: run apex-70b-fp16 for a 10% sample (spot check for edge-cases)
  * Metrics to capture: schema pass rate, token cost per request, 50/95/99 latency, and rate of re-prompts. We will push a short CSV with these after the run.

- Benchmarks and links
  * Public: https://redwood.ai/evals/novacare-20290531 (demo bench summary)
  * Internal perf: https://redwood.internal/run/novacare/20290531 (we'll give you sanitized CSV in Drive)

- Security artifacts
  * We'll attach a SOC2 summary and a short doc on Hosted vs Dedicated retention windows (Hosted: 30 days logs by default, can be configured; Dedicated: customer-managed retention).

I'll prepare an ops runbook for Monica to execute. Naomie, if you want I can include a minimal Postman collection for the idempotent function-call flow.

—Ben
